program_overview.title: Scratch Programming for Kids
program_overview.tagline: The best first coding language ever built, mastered properly: from the first dragged block to real games your child designed, in three focused months.
program_overview.description:
Scratch, built by MIT, is where millions of children write their first real program, and for good reason: logic is learned by snapping colorful blocks together, and the results move, sing and play back immediately. This live online course takes children aged 6 to 12 from zero to genuinely capable: 35+ projects across three months, from first animations to complete games with scores, levels, clones and multi-sprite coordination.

The pace is honest and kid-sized: two live classes a week plus 2 to 3 hours of playful practice completes the course in 3 months, and children who want more time take up to 4, the batch adapts. Every week ends with something to show the family; every month ends with a friendly mixed challenge that quietly revises earlier skills; and the course ends with a final project exam, a game demo plus a short viva, that decides the certificate. Real skills, real games, real pride.
what_makes_this_different: Every single week ships projects: 35+ games, animations and stories across the course, built by the child, not the teacher
Real Scratch depth: variables, lists, clones and broadcasts, the concepts that make later Python feel familiar
Kid-sized honest pace: 3 months at 2 classes a week, with a 4th month in hand for children who want more practice time
Monthly mixed challenges revise earlier skills on purpose, so nothing fades between weeks
A final project exam decides the certificate: a game demo plus a friendly viva, with a free retest after revision if needed
Small live batches capped at 10, grouped by age, with mini-batch and 1-on-1 options

learning_path.month_1: Foundations (Weeks 1-4): sprites, motion, sounds, events and first games, plus creative pen art
learning_path.month_2: Real game mechanics (Weeks 5-8): variables and scores, lists, clones, and multi-sprite games with broadcasts
learning_path.month_3: Mastery (Weeks 9-12): extensions and AI blocks, physics, polish, and the final capstone game presented at demo day

career_outcomes: A portfolio of 35+ Scratch projects crowned by an original capstone game
Computational thinking that shows up at school: sequencing, logic, debugging and patience
A confident step into our Kids Coding journey, Python for Kids or Minecraft and Roblox courses
A child who says "I made this" and can explain how it works

faqs.question: What will my child actually create in this Scratch course?
faqs.answer: Over 3 months your child builds 35+ real projects in Scratch: animations and interactive stories in month 1, genuine games with scores, clones and multi-sprite logic in month 2, and physics experiments, AI-block projects and a polished original capstone game in month 3. Every project is the child’s own work, demonstrated at home the same week it is built.

faqs.question: What age is this Scratch course right for?
faqs.answer: The course is designed for ages 6 to 12 and assumes zero coding experience. All your child needs is basic reading ability to follow on-screen labels; lessons are visual and hands-on, which suits younger learners especially well. Batches are grouped by age, so a 6-year-old is never racing an 11-year-old.

faqs.question: How long does it take a child to learn Scratch?
faqs.answer: To real capability, games with scores, levels, clones and logic, it takes most children 3 months at 2 live classes a week plus a little playful practice. The course keeps a 4th month in hand for children who want more repetition, with no rushing and no penalty. The very first animation happens in class one; the pride starts immediately.

faqs.question: How is my child assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No, and it is all gentle: classwork in every session, a small homework build after every class, and a monthly challenge that mixes new blocks with earlier ones so skills compound instead of fading. The course ends with a final exam, a capstone demo plus a friendly viva. Passing earns the certificate; a child who falls short gets focused revision and a free retest. Real knowledge, real projects, no empty badges.

faqs.question: Does my child need any coding background before joining?
faqs.answer: None at all. Scratch was created by MIT precisely for first-time coders: children snap colorful blocks together instead of typing code, so there is no syntax to memorize. The course starts from the very first block.

faqs.question: What software do we need, and does it cost anything?
faqs.answer: Only Scratch 3.0, which is completely free and runs in the web browser, so there is nothing to install or purchase. A regular computer or laptop with an internet connection is enough.

faqs.question: What comes after Scratch?
faqs.answer: Scratch builds the computational thinking that makes text-based languages far easier later. The course ends with a guided transition path toward typed code, and most students continue into our Python or web development courses when they are ready.

faqs.question: How much does the Scratch course cost?
faqs.answer: Group classes are ₹1,499 per month, which includes 2 live classes every week in a batch of at most 10 children. A mini batch of 3-4 students costs ₹2,999 per month, and personal 1-on-1 coaching with 2 private classes a week is ₹4,999 per month. International students pay a price set for their own country, shown on this page in their local currency.

faqs.question: Can we try a free class before enrolling?
faqs.answer: Yes, every child can take a free demo class first, with no commitment of any kind. Book a slot at learn.modernagecoders.com/contact, and you are welcome to sit in and watch; you can also reach us on WhatsApp at +91 91233 66161 with any questions.

faqs.question: Are classes live or pre-recorded?
faqs.answer: All classes are live 1-hour online sessions taught by a real teacher; we never use pre-recorded videos. Batches are small and interactive, so your child builds projects during class while the teacher watches and helps in real time.

faqs.question: Does my child receive a certificate at the end?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is earned, not handed out: the certificate is awarded on passing the final exam, a capstone game demo plus a friendly viva and a short mixed quiz, with a free retest after revision if the first attempt falls short. Alongside it stands the portfolio of 35+ real Scratch projects, which for most kids is the part they are proudest of.
